hints: Focus on which functional group is actually broken by dilute HCl, esters hydrolyse but alcohols do not.
Write out the acid hydrolysis for the ester options as carboxylic acid + alcohol, for example $\text{RCO}_2\text{R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{R'OH}$.
Find the molecular formula of each pair of products and simplify to the empirical formula to see which pair both reduce to the same simplest ratio.
walkthrough:
**Spot what can be hydrolysed**

Only esters (containing $\text{CO}_2$ linkage) are hydrolysed by $\text{HCl(aq)}$. Alcohols and diols are not hydrolysed.

General acid hydrolysis:
$$\text{RCO}_2\text{R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{R'OH}$$

**Eliminate the non-ester**

Option D, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is a diol with two $\text{OH}$ groups. It has no ester link to break, so it cannot be Q.

**Write the hydrolysis products for the esters**

For A $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
For B $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$$
For C $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Compare empirical formulas**

For B, the products are ethanoic acid, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$, and 3-hydroxypropanoic acid, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_3$.

Simplify both:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{O}$$
Both share the same empirical formula, so this is Q.

options.A: Hydrolysis gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$, empirical $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$) and $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$, empirical $\text{CH}_3\text{O}$). The H counts differ, so empirical formulas are not the same.
options.B: Hydrolysis gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$) and $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_3$). Both simplify to the same empirical formula $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$, so this fits the condition.
options.C: Hydrolysis gives propanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$) and propan-1-ol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$). One contains two O atoms and the other contains one O atom, so empirical formulas cannot match.
options.D: This is hexane-3,4-diol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It has no ester or other hydrolysable group, so it is not hydrolysed by $\text{HCl(aq)}$ at all.
